newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts hit in short-term - analysts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts hit in short-term - analysts.

text.p: The removal of Arnotts Ltd biscuits (cookies) from supermarket shelves as a result of an extortion threat would have a short-term earnings impact but the long-term effect was less certain, analysts said on Friday.
"It all depends on the length of time and that sort of thing. It could just be devastating," said a Melbourne-based analyst. "You saw what the peanut butter scare did to Kraft."
Philip Morris Cos Inc subsidiary Kraft Foods Ltd recalled some peanut butter products in Australia in June last year after a salmonella poisoning scare.
The episode was reported in local media to have cost Kraft at least A$6 million in lost sales over about two months.

A Sydney-based analyst said short-term earnings would be hit, but the scare should not affect the long-term valuation of the tightly-held company. Arnotts is about 70 percent owned by Campbell Soup Co of the United States.
"In the short-term earnings would be affected but the share price is not necessarily about short-term earnings," he said.
"It shouldn't really affect the share price that much."
The analysts said the impact would depend on any delay in consumers returning to the product once it was replaced on supermarket shelves.
The withdrawal could also give a short-term substitution boost to competitors such as George Weston Foods Ltd, one analyt said.

Arnotts has asked retailers in New South Wales and Queensland to remove its entire product range following a threat to poison Arnotts biscuits unless police involved in a murder investigation underwent lie detector tests.
Arnotts shares closed at A$8.45 on Thursday.
The biscuit maker requested a trading halt prior to the start of trade on Friday.
